notice: Package names are curated from distro knowledge and are NOT verified against live repositories (no network in the authoring environment). Every mapping carries a confidence level; see docs/distro-targets.md.

repos.name: RPM Fusion (free + nonfree)
repos.note: Needed for patent-encumbered codecs, Steam and the NVIDIA driver.

repos.name: Fedora COPR (community builds)
repos.note: Unofficial community builds; not reviewed by Fedora.

repos.name: Vendor RPM repository
repos.enable: Add the vendor's .repo file, then install by name
repos.note: Used for Chrome, VS Code, Docker CE and similar vendor-supplied builds.

repos.name: multilib
repos.enable: Uncomment the [multilib] section in /etc/pacman.conf, then sudo pacman -Sy
repos.note: Needed for 32-bit libraries used by Steam and Wine.

repos.name: Arch User Repository
repos.enable: Install an AUR helper (for example paru or yay), then paru -S {pkgs}
repos.note: Community-maintained build recipes; read the PKGBUILD before installing.

repos.name: Chaotic-AUR (prebuilt)
repos.enable: Optional prebuilt AUR binaries; follow chaotic.cx instructions

targets.name: Debian
targets.refresh_cmd: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get upgrade -y

repos.name: contrib / non-free / non-free-firmware
repos.enable: Add 'contrib non-free non-free-firmware' to the sources in /etc/apt/sources.list, then sudo apt-get update
repos.note: Needed for some firmware, drivers and proprietary packages.

repos.name: Vendor APT repository
repos.enable: Add the vendor's signing key and .list/.sources file, then apt-get update
repos.note: Used for Chrome, VS Code, Docker CE and similar vendor-supplied builds.

repos.name: bookworm/trixie-backports
repos.enable: Add the backports suite and install with -t <suite>-backports

targets.name: Ubuntu
targets.refresh_cmd: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get upgrade -y

repos.name: universe / multiverse
repos.enable: sudo add-apt-repository -y universe multiverse && sudo apt-get update
repos.note: Community and non-free packages; usually already enabled on desktop installs.

repos.name: Snap Store
repos.note: Preinstalled on Ubuntu; some apps (Firefox, Chromium) ship only as snaps.

repos.name: Personal Package Archive
repos.enable: sudo add-apt-repository -y ppa:{owner}/{name} && sudo apt-get update
repos.note: Unofficial; installs third-party software as root.

repos.name: Vendor APT repository
repos.enable: Add the vendor's signing key and .list/.sources file, then apt-get update
repos.note: Used for Chrome, VS Code, Docker CE and similar vendor-supplied builds.

repos.name: Packman
repos.enable: sudo zypper addrepo -cfp 90 https://ftp.gwdg.de/pub/linux/misc/packman/suse/openSUSE_Tumbleweed/ packman && sudo zypper dup --from packman --allow-vendor-change
repos.note: Multimedia codecs and extras not shipped by openSUSE for patent reasons.

repos.name: Open Build Service home/devel repo
repos.enable: sudo zypper addrepo -f {url} {alias} && sudo zypper refresh
repos.note: Community builds; not reviewed by openSUSE.

repos.name: Vendor RPM repository
repos.enable: Add the vendor's .repo file with zypper addrepo, then install by name
repos.note: Used for Chrome, VS Code, Docker CE and similar vendor-supplied builds.

fedora.text: Enable RPM Fusion free and nonfree before installing codecs, Steam or the NVIDIA driver.
For full video playback, swap ffmpeg-free for ffmpeg: sudo dnf swap ffmpeg-free ffmpeg --allowerasing.
NVIDIA driver is packaged as akmod-nvidia in RPM Fusion nonfree; with Secure Boot on, enroll the akmods key first.
Fedora uses SELinux; if a downloaded vendor app fails to start, check 'sudo ausearch -m avc -ts recent' before disabling anything.
Fedora's Flatpak remote is filtered; add the full Flathub remote: flatpak remote-add --if-not-exists flathub https://flathub.org/repo/flathub.flatpakrepo.

arch.text: Enable the multilib repository in /etc/pacman.conf before installing Steam, Wine or 32-bit games.
Packages marked source 'aur' are community recipes. Install an AUR helper and read each PKGBUILD first.
Never run 'pacman -Sy <pkg>' alone; always upgrade the whole system (pacman -Syu) to avoid partial upgrades.
Install flatpak first (sudo pacman -S flatpak) and add Flathub before using any flatpak mapping.
NVIDIA users: install nvidia-open (or nvidia-dkms for custom kernels) and nvidia-utils; lib32-nvidia-utils for Steam.

debian.text: Enable contrib, non-free and non-free-firmware in your APT sources for firmware and proprietary packages.
Debian stable ships conservative versions; use Flatpak or backports when you need a newer app.
Install flatpak and add Flathub before using any flatpak mapping: sudo apt-get install flatpak && flatpak remote-add --if-not-exists flathub https://flathub.org/repo/flathub.flatpakrepo.
Debian provides Firefox ESR as 'firefox-esr' rather than 'firefox'.
Debian's installer may not add your user to sudo; add it with 'su -c "usermod -aG sudo $USER"' and log in again.

ubuntu.text: Ubuntu's 'firefox' and 'chromium-browser' apt packages are transitional and install the snap; that is expected.
Install flatpak (sudo apt-get install flatpak) and add Flathub before using any flatpak mapping.
If a package is 'not found', enable universe/multiverse: sudo add-apt-repository universe multiverse.
Install ubuntu-restricted-extras for media codecs and Microsoft fonts.
NVIDIA users: use 'ubuntu-drivers install' to pick the right proprietary driver.

opensuse.text: Add the Packman repository and switch system multimedia packages to it for codecs.
openSUSE groups software in patterns; 'sudo zypper install -t pattern devel_basis' provides a compiler toolchain.
Install flatpak (sudo zypper install flatpak) and add Flathub before using any flatpak mapping.
Tumbleweed and Leap default to Btrfs with snapper snapshots; roll back from the boot menu if an update breaks the system.
NVIDIA drivers come from NVIDIA's own repository (zypper addrepo https://download.nvidia.com/opensuse/tumbleweed NVIDIA).
